name: Disfrutar
address: Carrer de Villarroel 163, 08036 Barcelona
tier: THE BERTHS · LA CRÈME — THE THREE-STAR HOUSES
recognition: World's 50 Best Restaurants No. 1, 2024
what_to_order: Panchino with caviar|Multi-spherical pesto with smoked eel and pistachio|Frozen gazpacho ice-cream sandwich
price_range: Call ahead: tasting menu EUR 315 (2026 editorial review, pairings from EUR 140) or about EUR 345 (2026 Barcelona guide) before wine
reservation: Online, about a year ahead; join the waiting list, which does move
notes: The panchino: a fried bun served warm and split to order, filled with cold beluga caviar and sour cream.
verdict: The rare kitchen that holds both titles at once: three MICHELIN stars from the November 2023 gala, then the World's 50 Best No. 1 in June 2024.
caveat: Two tasting menus only (Classic and Festival), no walk-ins, bookings open about a year out. Service days differ by source (Tue-Fri or Tue-Sat, lunch and dinner), so check the booking page for your date.

name: Cocina Hermanos Torres
address: Carrer del Taquígraf Serra 20, 08029 Barcelona
recognition: Three MICHELIN Stars since the November 2022 gala (2023 guide), kept in the 2026 Spain selection
what_to_order: Cebolla de Fuentes de Ebro|Maresme peas with acorn-fed ham and migas de pastor
price_range: Call ahead: tasting menu EUR 310 (Ara, Aug 2024) or EUR 295 plus EUR 175 pairing (Directo al Paladar, 2024); an undated 2026 travel guide says about EUR 170, which looks wrong
notes: ★ La cebolla de Fuentes de Ebro: the PDO onion caramelised 18 hours into a soup, finished with aged Parmesan and shaved black truffle — their homage to the father who grows it.
verdict: The only Barcelona three-star that puts its kitchen in the middle of the room — diners ring three live cooking stations instead of facing a wall that hides the cooks.
caveat: Tasting menu only, no a la carte, in Les Corts rather than the old town; book weeks ahead and confirm the current price, which sources put anywhere from EUR 295 to 310.

name: Lasarte
address: Carrer de Mallorca 259 (Monument Hotel), 08008 Barcelona
recognition: Three Michelin stars, the first awarded to any Barcelona restaurant (2017)
what_to_order: Millefeuille of smoked eel, foie gras and green apple|Ravioli with Osetra caviar and rosé champagne foam
notes: The "1995" millefeuille: smoked eel, foie gras, spring onion and a caramelised crackle, with a green-apple snap that cuts the fat.
verdict: Barcelona's first kitchen to win three Michelin stars (2017), and it has held all three every year since — but the hand plating Berasategui's classics belongs to Paolo Casagrande, born in the Veneto, not Berasategui himself, whose name the restaurant carries.
caveat: Dinner tasting about EUR 345, lunch about EUR 225 (prices from the old record, not re-checked); smart dress, book weeks ahead. Recent listings show it closed Sunday to Tuesday, and Berasategui is rarely in the Barcelona room.

name: Enigma
address: Carrer de Sepúlveda 38–40, 08015 Barcelona
recognition: Two MICHELIN stars, 2026 Guide Espana (awarded 25 November 2025, Malaga gala)
what_to_order: Cold almond and bonito soup|Earl Grey ravioli|Non-alcoholic pairing
price_range: EUR 260 menu from Sept 2025 (Ara, Nov 2025; Adrià said it might rise in January 2026); wine pairing EUR 160, non-alcoholic EUR 90
reservation: Wed–Fri eves only, book via enigmaconcept.es
notes: The 25-course menu itself: cold almond-bonito soup, Earl Grey ravioli, room after shifting room.
verdict: Albert Adria's only surviving Barcelona restaurant: a tasting menu of roughly 25 courses, served evenings and never a la carte, that won a second Michelin star in November 2025 — having first earned one back in 2017.
caveat: Tasting menu only, about four hours, no walk-ins, and the full price is charged for late cancellation or no-show (old record: inside 72 hours). Nights shift by season, so book through enigmaconcept.es weeks out.

name: Dos Palillos
address: Carrer d'Elisabets, 9, El Raval (Ciutat Vella), 08001 Barcelona
recognition: Second Repsol Sun in the 2026 Repsol Guide, the only Barcelona restaurant to add a Sun this year; also holds one MICHELIN Star (per May 2026 listings)
what_to_order: Shiitake and scallion gyoza|Nippon burger|Black truffle mochi|Wagyu terimochi
notes: Steamer of shiitake-and-scallion gyoza with black sesame, dipped in soy — a tasting-menu signature
verdict: Holds a current one-MICHELIN-star rating not for a dining room but for a small open-kitchen counter where former elBulli head chef Albert Raurich runs Spanish tapas through a Japanese-led Asian lens as a surprise tasting menu.
caveat: The starred meal is the small counter at the back: surprise tasting menu only, fixed seatings, books out. The sake bar at the entrance is first-come, a la carte and a different experience.

name: Suculent
address: Rambla del Raval 45, 08001 Barcelona (MICHELIN, The Infatuation; some listings give 43)
recognition: MICHELIN Guide listed (a Plate), not starred
what_to_order: Steak tartare on grilled marrow bone|Duck croquette|Smoked eel with beetroot beurre blanc|Catalan-style baby broad beans
notes: Steak tartare hand-cut over grilled marrow bone, crowned with shattering pommes soufflees.
verdict: The steak tartare on grilled marrow bone here is the original Toni Romero plated in 2012, not one of the copies that now turn up on menus across Spain.
caveat: A tight split-level room; the few tables book out, and with sharing plates the bill climbs past a cheap night out. Opening days differ between listings, so check before you walk over.

name: Mont Bar
address: Carrer de la Diputació 220, 08011 Barcelona
recognition: Two MICHELIN Stars, awarded at the November 2025 Malaga gala (first star since 2023)
what_to_order: Sobrasada and Mahón cheese mochi|Quisquilla vol-au-vent|Clam soufflé|Pigeon and cacao
price_range: Tasting menus about EUR 190 (Classic) to EUR 240 (2026 sources); a la carte snacks and mains also available
notes: Sobrasada, walnut and Mahon mochi: chewy rice skin giving way to warm cured-pork ooze, cut by salt-sharp island cheese.
verdict: The snacks, not the formal plates, are the reason to come to this two-star (promoted November 2025) — load up on the aperitivo-format dishes and treat the mains as a postscript.
caveat: Book well ahead now it holds two stars; the kitchen-front marble counter puts you in the cooks' noise. A la carte needs at least three snacks and two mains, so it is not a quick drink stop.
hot_this_month: Promoted to two stars in November 2025; the 2027 MICHELIN Spain list comes out on 24 Nov 2026, so book before then (checked 15 Oct 2026).

name: Aleia
address: Passeig de Gràcia 132, 08008 Barcelona
recognition: Two MICHELIN stars, awarded at the Guide Spain & Andorra 2026 gala in Malaga, 25 Nov 2025 (first star Nov 2022)
what_to_order: Palamós red prawn with piriñaca|Isla Cristina langoustines with amontillado beurre blanc|Scallops in cava sauce|Beef fillet with patates pebrots
price_range: About EUR 187-200 for the 14-course menu; about EUR 320 with pairing (reviews; no official 2026 figure found)
notes: Palamos red prawns over piriñaca — sweet Costa Brava shellfish cut by the tomato-pepper-onion bite of a Cadiz chopped salad, pooled with a green-pepper gazpacho.
verdict: A rare Barcelona two-star where the register is Cadiz, not Catalan — sherry, almadraba tuna and piriñaca threaded through Palamos prawns and Mediterranean produce — inside Domenech i Montaner's Casa Fuster on Passeig de Gracia.
caveat: Tasting menu only, around EUR 200 before wine (about EUR 320 with the pairing); book the Casa Fuster dining room weeks ahead. A reserve-and-dress-up evening, not a walk-in.

name: Cinc Sentits
address: Carrer d'Entença 60, 08015 Barcelona
recognition: Two MICHELIN stars: first 2008, second at the end of 2020 (2021 guide); still two-star in 2026
what_to_order: Maple shot|Hour-roasted sweet potato|Quail eggs cooked 100 seconds
notes: The opening shot, his ode to Canada: warm maple syrup, chilled cream, cava sabayon and rock salt, layered in a glass and thrown back in one — heat striking cold in a single swallow.
verdict: Of Barcelona's two-star tables, the one whose chef never trained in a kitchen — Jordi Artal ran tech in Silicon Valley before this, and his seasonal tasting menus repeat no principal ingredient twice.
caveat: No a la carte: two seasonal tasting menus, Light (about EUR 189) and Tasting (about EUR 219), prices from the old record. Book three to four weeks out.

name: Kamikaze
address: Carrer del Rosselló 197, L'Antiga Esquerra de l'Eixample, 08036 Barcelona
tier: THE NEW GUARD — THIS YEAR'S STAR AND BIBS
recognition: First MICHELIN star, Guía España 2026 — one of 25 new one-stars awarded at the 25 Nov 2025 gala in Málaga (SOHRLIN Andalucía), barely three years after opening as a vermutería.
what_to_order: Cabracho a la plancha with ponzu butter|Sea-urchin mochi|Natto catalán|Pandan prawn|Asparagus with miso and strawberry
price_range: Call ahead: tasting menus from EUR 75 (Directo al Paladar listing) or EUR 85 (same article's headline); old record says EUR 75-95
notes: Cabracho a la plancha glossed in ponzu butter — smoky, citric, silky; the house "plato estrella."
verdict: A three-year-old, 28-seat Eixample restaurant — small dining rooms, no à la carte — that climbed from vermutería to a first Michelin star in the 2026 guide on tasting menus starting around €75, the accessible-value entry to Barcelona's new-star class.
caveat: 28 seats, tasting menus only, no a la carte; it is no longer the casual vermouth stop it began as. Menus rotate with the season, and the new star means booking ahead.

name: Glug
address: Carrer de Viladomat 289, Esquerra de l'Eixample, 08029 Barcelona — opposite the Sant Jordi swimming pool
tier: THE NEW GUARD — THIS YEAR'S STAR AND BIBS
recognition: New Bib Gourmand, 2026 MICHELIN Guide España — a first-time entry roughly 17-18 months after opening
what_to_order: Onion soup with Comté buttons|Rabbit meatballs|Beatrice Casella's desserts|Natural wine by the glass
notes: Onion soup with Comté-filled "buttons" — French comfort rebuilt with Catalan-Italian nerve.
verdict: Glug earned a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 Michelin Guide España barely 18 months after its June 2024 opening — a genuine, cross-verified fast-track, not hype.
caveat: Tiny (about 38 seats, mostly at the bar) with erratic hours (closed Tue/Wed, several days dinner-only), so seats go fast now the Bib landed; and the headline "620-plus" wine count is unverified — Michelin and Star Wine List describe the list as smaller, nearer 280 references.

name: Oníric
address: Carrer de Rabassa 37, Gràcia, 08024 Barcelona, Spain
tier: THE NEW GUARD — THIS YEAR'S STAR AND BIBS
recognition: New Bib Gourmand in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide España (announced Nov 2025) — earned within about two years of opening, one of ~5 Catalan additions
what_to_order: Conger-eel buñuelos with green curry, coconut and tamarind|Herrén menu|Somni menu
price_range: Tasting menus EUR 18-36 depending on the sitting (Nació Digital, Nov 2025)
notes: Conger-eel buñuelos bathed in green curry, coconut and tamarind — crisp, fragrant, deliberately risky.
verdict: One of Barcelona's strongest sub-€50 tasting menus — a modern-Catalan room that earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand within roughly two years of opening.
caveat: Tiny (roughly six tables), so it books out weeks ahead; the full Somni tasting menu must be requested at booking and requires the whole table, and the ~€24-26 Herrén bargain is weekday-lunch only.

name: Can Culleretes
address: Carrer de Quintana 5, 08002 Barcelona
recognition: Founded 1786 — oldest restaurant in Catalonia and second-oldest in Spain after Madrid's Casa Botin (1725); Guinness-cited as Barcelona's oldest
what_to_order: Canelons 'els de sempre'|Roast duck with prunes|Wild boar stew|Botifarra amb mongetes|Crema catalana
notes: Canelons "els de sempre": veal-and-pork tubes under nutmeg bechamel, gratinated with Emmental — first served in the 1950s, now up to 300 plates on a Sunday.
verdict: Catalonia's oldest dining room (1786) still turns out its canelons and duck-with-prunes from house recipes — come for the unbroken lineage and the EUR 18-20 menu del dia, not for cooking that out-thinks the city's modern kitchens.
caveat: Closed Mondays; a warren of tiled, photo-hung rooms that fills with tour groups. Hearty, generous Catalan tradition, not refined plating.
hot_this_month: Canelons from the house recipe, the Catalan dish of Sant Esteve, are the cold-weather order; lunch Tue–Sun (checked 15 Oct 2026).

name: 7 Portes (Set Portes)
address: Passeig d'Isabel II 14, 08003 Barcelona
recognition: Cafè de les 7 Portes opened 1836 in Xifré's arcaded block; a full restaurant since 1929
what_to_order: Arròs Parellada|Bacallà|Xató|Canelons
price_range: Group menus EUR 52 and EUR 69 (May 2026); a la carte past EUR 40 a head
notes: Arròs Parellada: saffron rice with prawns, chicken and butifarra sausage, every shell and bone already lifted out.
verdict: The dining room opened as a café in 1836, but the kitchen only fired up in 1929 — so the shell-off arròs Parellada the house is known for was neither born here (Café Suís plated the first one, around 1902) nor is it the city's finest paella; you come for the seven salons and the live piano, not a revelation on the plate.
caveat: Reserve ahead: this is a tourist landmark as much as a kitchen, a meal lands past EUR 40 a head, and the seven salons run loud and full — don't mistake the history for cutting-edge cooking.

name: Els Quatre Gats
address: Carrer de Montsió, 3 bis, Barri Gòtic, 08002 Barcelona
recognition: Casa Martí (Puig i Cadafalch, 1895-96) is listed as a Bé Cultural d'Interès Nacional (BCIN) in the Catalan heritage register.
what_to_order: Canelons 4 Gats|Esqueixada|Monkfish tail with potatoes|Pig's trotters|Millefeuille
notes: Canelons 4 Gats: the house meat cannelloni gratinated under béchamel, the kitchen's self-declared specialty.
verdict: A BCIN-listed national-heritage landmark you come for Puig i Cadafalch's modernista room (café opened 1897, building 1895-96) and the Picasso history, not for cooking that ranks among Barcelona's best.
caveat: The room outclasses the plate for many diners (OpenTable reviews 2025-26 are mixed), prices run high and the crowd skews tourist; book at weekends, as the staff discourage look-only visits.

name: Bar Cañete
address: Carrer de la Unió 17, 08001 Barcelona
tier: THE BERTHS · AT THE COUNTER — THE TAPAS BARS
recognition: Listed in The World's 50 Best Discovery (Barcelona)
what_to_order: Tortillitas de camarones|Croquetas de jamón|Jamón carved to order|Toasted tomato flatbread|Arroz de marisco
reservation: Book for tables; counter stools are walk-in and Infatuation reports ~30-minute queues
notes: ★ Tortillitas de camarones — Cádiz shrimp fritters fried to a lacy chickpea-flour gold; then the jamón croquetas.
verdict: Skip the back dining room with its dark wood and red leather — the long bar over the open kitchen is the seat to queue for. The tortillitas de camarones reach you straight from the oil, lacy and blistering at the edges, and the cook carving jamón an arm's length off is half the meal.
caveat: Roughly EUR 35-55 a head at dinner, counter stools walk-in only, closed Sundays. The cooking is Andalusian, not Catalan, despite the Raval address.

name: Cal Pep
address: Plaça de les Olles, 8, El Born / La Ribera, Ciutat Vella, 08003 Barcelona
tier: AT THE COUNTER — THE TAPAS BARS
recognition: Listed on The World's 50 Best Discovery (50 Best's curated directory, not the live annual ranking); the same page claims it once reached No. 31 on the main list — single source, no year given, hedged. Also listed by OAD Guides and reviewed by The Infatuation.
what_to_order: Truita (tortilla) with aioli and chorizo|Tuna tartare|Fried small fish and shellfish of the day
reservation: Counter walk-in only; bookings for the back room and larger groups
notes: Oozing, molten-centred Spanish tortilla finished with aioli and chorizo
verdict: A no-menu, no-bookings seafood counter open since 1989 where Pep's cooks pick your plates — touristy now, but the molten tortilla and tuna tartare still draw a queue before the doors open.
caveat: Not a place to linger or budget tightly: the counter takes no bookings (only a small back dining room does), lines form before opening, it is heavily touristed, the market-priced seafood can climb fast, and you cede all menu choice to the cooks.

name: Quimet & Quimet
address: Carrer del Poeta Cabanyes 25, 08004 Barcelona
tier: AT THE COUNTER — THE TAPAS BARS
recognition: Bodega founded 1914, run by the same family for five generations
what_to_order: Salmon, Greek yogurt and truffled honey montadito|Ibérico pork cheek in escabeche montadito|Foie, mushroom and chestnut montadito|A glass from the house bottles
notes: Montadito of smoked salmon, tangy Greek yogurt and truffled honey on crisp bread — salt, smoke, floral sweetness in two bites.
verdict: A wine bodega since 1914 that still makes you eat standing at the counter — order the salmon-and-truffled-honey montadito and you are tasting a house best-seller, not a Carrer Blai imitation of it.
caveat: Heads up — standing room only, no chairs, no bookings; closed weekends and the whole of August, and a queue forms before the noon and 6pm openings. Come right at open.

name: La Cova Fumada
address: Carrer del Baluard 56, 08003 Barcelona
recognition: Founded 1944, Barceloneta; birthplace of la bomba (1950s)
what_to_order: La bomba|Sardines on the grill|Carxofes|Chocitos and calamari
notes: La bomba: a crisp-fried potato sphere stuffed with spiced meat, slicked with all-i-oli and a fierce red salsa picante.
verdict: Barcelona's bomba was born in this kitchen — eat the original at a marble table, not the frozen replicas reheated on tourist terraces.
caveat: Cash only, no sign on the door, marble tables, mostly daytime hours (roughly 9am to mid-afternoon, with a short Thursday-Friday evening service), shut Sundays, and the queue forms before a table opens.
hot_this_month: Closed Sundays, so not on 25 Oct or Tots Sants (1 Nov 2026); go Mon–Fri 09:00–15:30 or Saturday to 14:30 for the bomba (checked 15 Oct 2026).

name: El Vaso de Oro
address: Carrer de Balboa, 6, La Barceloneta, 08003 Barcelona
recognition: Guía Repsol Solete: the guide's mark for characterful everyday places; it names the solomillo con foie and the house beer
what_to_order: Solomillo con foie|Cerveza Fort|Fish and shellfish from the bar card
notes: Solomillo con foie: seared beef fillet under a slice of hot, melting foie gras
verdict: Time Out Barcelona gives this 1962 Barceloneta cervecería a full 5/5, and the order the local crowd reaches for is the solomillo con foie, not the tapas.
caveat: Not a sit-down dinner: no reservations, only a few stools, elbow-to-elbow at the bar, and Barceloneta's tourist crowds mean queues. The house Fort beer is, per the venue's own history, brewed at a microbrewery in L'Hospitalet rather than on the premises.

name: Els Pescadors
address: Plaça de Prim 1, 08005 Barcelona
recognition: A restaurant since 1980 in a fishermen's tavern dating to 1913, on Plaça de Prim, Poblenou
what_to_order: Fishermen's bomba rice|Suquet de peix|Arròs a banda|Arroz caldoso de bogavante
notes: Bomba fishermen's rice (~EUR 27.50): Valencian bomba cooked to a starchy bite, three fish straight off the day's auction.
verdict: The Poblenou rice house locals book the ombú terrace for — fish in daily off the Arenys de Mar auction, not the beachfront paella the tour groups queue for.
caveat: Special-occasion prices (~EUR 50-60 a head, not a chiringuito), and the terrace tables go first, so book ahead. The gnarled trees shading the square are ombú brought from South America, not figs.
hot_this_month: The terrace on Plaça de Prim still works for an October lunch while the sea averages about 21°C; book weekends (checked 15 Oct 2026).

name: El Xampanyet
address: Carrer de Montcada 22, 08003 Barcelona
recognition: Family bar, established 1929 — three generations of the Ninou family
what_to_order: House xampanyet|Anchovies in vinegar|House cava
notes: A glass of the house xampanyet — slightly sparkling, gently sweet — with a saucer of their marinated anchovies in vinegar.
verdict: The pour to order is the cloudy, faintly sweet house xampanyet, bottled on the premises and poured from the bottle — not the cava list. The bar took its name from that wine in the sixties, and it still makes its own.
caveat: No reservations, and a standing-room crush at the tiled marble counter; it leans cash-and-quick. Come right on opening or wait shoulder to shoulder.

name: Bar Bodega Quimet
address: Carrer de Vic, 23, Gràcia, 08006 Barcelona
recognition: Listed as a Solete in the Guía Repsol — the guide's mark for characterful, unpretentious everyday spots worth the trip.
what_to_order: Barrel vermut|Cantabrian anchovies|Berberechos|Navajas
price_range: About EUR 10-20 a head for vermut and conservas (guide estimate)
reservation: 1954 Gràcia bodega of marble and hydraulic tile, preserved by the Montero brothers, pouring barrel vermut.
notes: Barrel-poured house vermut, chased with a tin of Cantabrian anchovies or berberecho cockles.
verdict: A genuinely preserved 1954 Gràcia vermut bodega — barrel vermut and tinned conservas at bar prices, the room the Monteros kept rather than gutted, and not the Poble-sec Quimet & Quimet.
caveat: A small marble-tabled room that fills fast at the weekend vermut hour; the card leans on tins and cold variados over a full hot kitchen.

name: Morro Fi
address: Carrer del Consell de Cent 171, 08015 Barcelona (La Nova Esquerra de l'Eixample, corner of Comte Borrell)
recognition: Began as a Barcelona bar-crawl/aperitiu blog in 2007; the first bar opened at Consell de Cent 171 in 2011, and its own De Muller-bottled house vermut and conservas line followed from 2012.
what_to_order: House vermut on ice|Potato chip with pickled mussel|Banderillas|House conservas
notes: House De Muller-bottled vermut over ice, with a thick potato chip crowned by a pickled mussel, plus banderillas and tinned conservas.
verdict: A tiny standing-room vermuteria that turned a 2007 bar-crawl blog into the template most new-wave Barcelona vermut bars now copy; if you want a seat or a quiet drink, this is the wrong bar.
caveat: Room for barely fifteen inside — standing-only, no reservations, packed at vermut hour; expect to drink out on the pavement.

name: Bar Mut
address: Carrer de Pau Claris, 192, L'Eixample, 08037 Barcelona, Spain
recognition: The Infatuation (Barcelona) carries a full review: a classic, cramped Eixample wine bar priced $$$$ with no numeric score; the write-up warns it is neither quick nor budget-friendly but praises the wine-with-tapas pairing. (No verbatim quote — the original card's quotation was not in the review.)
what_to_order: Huevos fritos montadito|Lobster with egg and brandy|Steak with foie or mushrooms|Seasonal croquettes|A glass from the list
reservation: Takes reservations (OpenTable per The Infatuation); fills fast
notes: Huevos fritos: runny poached egg, prawn, matchstick fried potato and chorizo sauce on a montadito.
verdict: More refined and more expensive than Barcelona's standing-bar tapas classics: a wine-first Eixample room open since June 2005 whose 300-plus-bottle list backs a daily chalkboard of market tapas.
caveat: Not quick and not budget-friendly; the cramped marble standing bar takes reservations but fills fast, and the bill climbs with every glass.

name: Can Cisa / Bar Brutal
address: Carrer de la Princesa 14 (bar entrance on Carrer Barra de Ferro 1), El Born – La Ribera, 08003 Barcelona
recognition: Opened 2013 as one of the pioneers of Barcelona's natural-wine (vin vivant) scene, on the El Born / La Ribera edge
what_to_order: Chicken gizzards with ponzu and watercress|Anchovies in olive oil|Pata negra jamón|A bottle off the Can Cisa shelves
notes: Chicken gizzards with ponzu and watercress, tender, tangy, gently offal-funky, with a chilled natural red.
verdict: The natural-wine list is among the deepest and most low-intervention in Barcelona; the short seasonal tapas menu is honest but plays second fiddle to what's in the glass.
caveat: No longer the walk-in free-for-all it once was: lunch and dinner tables must be booked with a bank card (about €20 per person no-show fee), and walk-ins are for drinks only; the bar is tiny and the El Born street is touristy.

name: Els Sortidors del Parlament
address: Carrer del Parlament 53, Sant Antoni (L'Eixample), 08015 Barcelona, Spain
recognition: A December 12, 2012 Barcelona Sights post flagged it as a new bodega on Carrer del Parlament, pouring wine at shop prices plus a small de-corking fee inside a former ~250m2 motorbike workshop; the operating company Els Sortidors del Parlament SL was later constituted in January 2017.
what_to_order: Vermut de grifo|Cured cheese board|Catalan conserves|Embotits
notes: House vermut de grifo over an upturned barrel, plus the cured-cheese and Catalan conserves board.
verdict: A bottle here costs its wine-shop shelf price plus a flat ~4 euro corkage rather than a restaurant markup, so you drink further up the list for the same money than at a table-service wine bar on the same street.
caveat: Closed Tuesdays (open Mondays); small and busy at weekends; shop bottles carry a ~4 euro corkage on top of the shelf price.

name: Granja M. Viader
address: Carrer d'en Xuclà, 4-6, 08001 Barcelona (El Raval)
recognition: Granja trading since 1870, Viader family since c.1904; Cacaolat patented here December 1931; fifth generation owner from 7 May 2026 (Ara)
what_to_order: Suizo|Melindros|Mel i mató|House crema catalana
notes: The suizo: spoon-thick hot chocolate under a cold cap of fresh whipped cream, melindros to dip.
verdict: The reputed birthplace of Cacaolat still pours a spoon-thick, cream-capped suizo in a wood-panelled room little changed in generations — but it closes Sundays, Mondays and every midday, so it is easy to miss.
caveat: Closed Sundays and Mondays, and every day at midday (roughly 13:15–17:00); a small wood-panelled room where tourist queues form. Note that the bottled Cacaolat brand long ago left the family — now owned by the Damm group — so what you drink here is the house chocolate, not the commercial bottle.
hot_this_month: Thick chocolate weather returns once the clocks go back on 25 Oct 2026: the cup of chocolate and mel i mató are the order (checked 15 Oct 2026).

name: Caelum
address: Carrer de la Palla, 8, Ciutat Vella, 08002 Barcelona, Spain
recognition: Listed in Time Out Barcelona's El Gotic shopping guide (2017) — an editorial listing, not a starred pick or award.
what_to_order: Hot chocolate|Yemas de Santa Teresa|Convent marzipan|Cider cake from Santa Inés, Seville|Trappist beer
notes: Thick nun-made hot chocolate with convent marzipan and Santa Teresa egg-yolk yemas
verdict: Not a restaurant but a cloistered-convent sweets cafe: you eat nun-made marzipan and monastery hot chocolate in a candlelit basement set among the remains of the Gothic Quarter's medieval baths.
caveat: Not a meal: only convent sweets, chocolate and tea, so don't come for lunch. The candlelit basement has few tables and fills fast, and the stones below are unsettled ground — variously described as a medieval Jewish women's mikveh or older public/Roman baths.
hot_this_month: The basement over the medieval baths comes into its own as the evenings cool: convent marzipan and hot chocolate, a fit for the Tots Sants week (checked 15 Oct 2026).

name: Pastisseria Escribà (Antiga Casa Figueras)
address: La Rambla, 83, Ciutat Vella, 08002 Barcelona, Spain
recognition: On Barcelona's official Ruta del Modernisme and listed by Barcelona City Council (meet.barcelona); the 1902 modernista shopfront directed by Antoni Ros i Güell, with mosaics, stained glass and stucco.
what_to_order: Cremadet|Croissants and pastries from the counter
notes: Cremadet — crisp puff pastry filled with lemon-scented crema catalana, caramelized to a brittle top.
verdict: The listed 1902 modernista room, not the pastry, is why you stop — order a cremadet, take in the Ros i Güell mosaics, and expect a counter, not a meal.
caveat: On the busiest stretch of La Rambla beside La Boqueria; a pastry counter with a small terrace, not a restaurant. The Rambla pavement works closed it for five months in 2025 and a second closure from mid-January 2026 was announced; no reopening date was found, so check before going.
hot_this_month: Panellets week: Escribà's pine-nut panellets are among the city's best by Time Out's count; buy before Tots Sants on Sun 1 Nov 2026 (checked 15 Oct 2026).

name: Bar La Plata
address: Carrer de la Mercè, 28, 08002 Barcelona (Barri Gòtic)
tier: STANDING UP — ONE THING, DONE FOR DECADES
recognition: The same four tapas — small fried fish, anchovies, butifarra sausage and a tomato-onion-olive salad — served from one marble-countered Gothic Quarter room since 1945.
what_to_order: Pescadito frito|Anchoas|Botifarra|Tomato, onion and olive salad|Barrel wine from Penedès
notes: Pescadito frito — small whole fish fried hot and crisp, about €2.50–3.50, with house vermut or wine from the barrel.
verdict: A ritual, not a meal: the same four tapas since 1945 — fried fish, anchovies, butifarra and tomato-onion salad — eaten mostly standing at a marble counter, with no printed menu and no choice beyond those four, though the roughly €2.50–3.50 plates and barrel wine reward the crush.
caveat: No reservations, no printed menu, only four tapas, and mostly standing in one small, packed room; closed Sundays.

name: Can Paixano (La Xampanyeria)
address: Carrer de la Reina Cristina, 7, Ciutat Vella (Port Vell), 08003 Barcelona
tier: STANDING UP — ONE THING, DONE FOR DECADES
recognition: Pouring its own Berenguer Ramon cava to a standing-room crowd since 1969
what_to_order: Cava rosat|Botifarra bocadillo|Brut cava
notes: The deep-pink house cava (Rosat) by the glass, with a warm grilled botifarra bocadillo
verdict: A glass of the house cava still costs barely over a euro and there is nowhere to sit — you drink it standing at the counter or not at all.
caveat: Cash is easiest; standing-only, no table service and no reservations. Open Mon–Sat, most crowded roughly 7–10:30pm, closed Sundays.

name: Bar Tomás (El Tomás de Sarrià)
address: Carrer Major de Sarrià 49, 08017 Barcelona (Sarrià-Sant Gervasi)
tier: STANDING UP — ONE THING, DONE FOR DECADES
recognition: Time Out Barcelona calls its allioli-led patatas bravas the best in the city, noting the sauce sits closer to a garlicky allioli than the usual spicy brava sauce (verified Jul 2026).
what_to_order: Patatas bravas|Tuna empanadillas|Cantabrian anchovies
notes: Patatas bravas: craggy fried potato wedges under garlicky allioli streaked with chili-hot oil
verdict: The reason to climb up to Sarrià is the bravas: craggy hand-cut fried potato wedges under a garlic allioli cut with a separate hot oil, not the usual spicy tomato sauce, which Time Out ranks among Barcelona's best.
caveat: Not a destination for the room: a plain, cramped stand-up bar in uptown Sarrià, all function over ambience; it's closed Sundays (Monday–Saturday only) and you'll likely queue for a plate that now pulls as many tourists as locals.

name: Bacoa Kiosko
address: Av. del Marquès de l'Argentera, 1, El Born / La Ribera, 08003 Barcelona
recognition: Time Out Barcelona, 'The best burgers in the city' guide — Bacoa is the lead entry, its three locations opening the list; also Time Out Barcelona 'Best Sandwich' award winner, 2010.
what_to_order: The Bacoa burger|Asturiana|Hand-cut chips
notes: The house Bacoa: stone-grilled patty, smoked bacon, manchego, cheddar, pickles, artisan mustard, smoky char.
verdict: It is the lead entry in Time Out Barcelona's burger guide and won the magazine's 2010 Best Sandwich award, but the independent 15-seat 2010 pioneer is now flagged closed and the brand survives as an AmRest-owned mini-chain (the operator of Burger King and Pizza Hut Spain).
caveat: A small counter spot with no reservations, so expect a queue. Time Out flags the original "Little Bacoa" (Colomines, 2) as closed; the still-open Born door is the Kiosko on Av. del Marquès de l'Argentera, 1, which is AmRest-run rather than the independent original.

name: Flash Flash
address: Carrer de la Granada del Penedes 25, Sant Gervasi-Galvany, 08006 Barcelona
recognition: Named a Guia Repsol Solete, the guide's seal for beloved, good-value casual eateries
what_to_order: Tortilla de patatas|Flash Flash burger
notes: The tortilla de patatas de toda la vida, the plain classic among fifty-plus versions
verdict: You come for the near-intact 1970 room and its Karin Leiz wall images, not for cooking that beats a good neighbourhood bar: the tortillas are competent rather than revelatory and, at roughly EUR 20-30 a head, priced above a corner-bar omelette.
caveat: Uptown in residential Sant Gervasi-Galvany, off the tourist trail; pricey for what is essentially an omelette (roughly EUR 20-30 a head, under EUR 35 per Guia Repsol); takes no reservations, first-come-first-served, so arrive early. Not a gourmet destination.
